Ruth 1.summary: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine sends Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and their sons Mahlon and Chilion from Bethlehem in Judah to Moab (Ruth 1:1–2). Elimelech dies, the sons marry the Moabite women Orpah and Ruth, and after about ten years both sons die, leaving three widows (Ruth 1:3–5). Naomi hears that the LORD has given his people bread, so she starts for Judah and urges her daughters-in-law to go home to their mothers (Ruth 1:6–13). Orpah kisses Naomi and goes back, but Ruth clings to her and promises, "thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God" (Ruth 1:14–18). The women reach Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest, and Naomi asks to be called Mara, which means bitter, because the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with her (Ruth 1:19–22).
Ruth 1.whereWeAre: Judges 21 ended with Israel doing what was right in its own eyes, and Ruth begins "in the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1). This chapter follows Naomi's loss in Moab and Ruth's choice to go home with her to Bethlehem. Chapter 2 shows how the two widows find food there.

keyFigures.name: Naomi
keyFigures.role: Loses her husband and both sons in Moab, then returns to Bethlehem and says the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with her.

keyFigures.name: Ruth
keyFigures.role: A Moabitess who clings to Naomi and chooses Naomi's people and Naomi's God.

keyFigures.name: Orpah
keyFigures.role: Kisses Naomi and goes back to her own people.

keyFigures.name: Elimelech, Mahlon, and Chilion
keyFigures.role: A husband and two sons who move to Moab during a famine and die there.

keyFigures.name: The women of Bethlehem
keyFigures.role: Ask, "Is this Naomi?" when she comes home.

keyFigures.name: The LORD
keyFigures.role: Gives his people bread again, though Naomi feels his hand has gone out against her.

keyThemes.explanation: Ruth stays with Naomi even though Naomi urges her to go home: "whither thou goest, I will go."
Naomi does not hide her pain. She asks to be called Mara, "for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me."
Ruth leaves Moab and makes Naomi's people and Naomi's God her own.
The chapter ends "in the beginning of barley harvest," a small sign that bread and hope are coming back.

Ruth 2.summary: Naomi has a relative of her husband's named Boaz, a wealthy man, and Ruth goes out to glean after the reapers and comes to a part of the field that belongs to Boaz (Ruth 2:1–3). Boaz greets his reapers, learns who Ruth is from his servant, and tells her to stay close to his maidens, who have been told not to touch her, and to drink from the vessels the young men have filled (Ruth 2:4–9). Ruth asks why she has found grace in his eyes when she is a stranger, and Boaz answers that he has heard all she has done for her mother-in-law and asks the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings she has come to trust, to reward her (Ruth 2:10–13). At mealtime he gives her parched corn, and he tells his young men to let her glean among the sheaves and to leave handfuls on purpose for her (Ruth 2:14–16). Ruth beats out about an ephah of barley and brings it home with the food she saved, and Naomi blesses the man and says he is "one of our next kinsmen" (Ruth 2:17–20). Ruth stays with the maidens of Boaz to the end of the barley and wheat harvests (Ruth 2:21–23).
Ruth 2.whereWeAre: Chapter 1 ended with Naomi and Ruth arriving in Bethlehem at the start of barley harvest. Now Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz, who protects her and makes sure she has plenty. Chapter 3 turns Naomi's hope for Ruth into a bold plan at the threshing floor.

keyFigures.name: Ruth
keyFigures.role: Gleans from morning until evening to feed herself and Naomi.

keyFigures.name: Boaz
keyFigures.role: A wealthy relative of Elimelech who protects Ruth and tells his men to leave extra grain for her.

keyFigures.name: Naomi
keyFigures.role: Blesses Boaz and says he is "one of our next kinsmen."

keyFigures.name: The servant over the reapers
keyFigures.role: Tells Boaz that Ruth is "the Moabitish damsel" who came back with Naomi.

keyFigures.name: The reapers and young men
keyFigures.role: Answer Boaz, "The LORD bless thee," and are told not to touch or rebuke Ruth.

keyThemes.explanation: Ruth gleans after the reapers, as the poor were allowed to do, and Boaz makes sure she is safe and has plenty.
Ruth works "from the morning until now" with only a short rest, and she brings home about an ephah of barley.
Boaz welcomes Ruth even though she is "a stranger" from Moab.
Naomi says the LORD "hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead" through Boaz.

Ruth 3.summary: Naomi tells Ruth to wash, anoint herself, put on her clothes, and go down to the threshing floor where Boaz is winnowing barley; after he has eaten and drunk, Ruth is to uncover his feet and lie down (Ruth 3:1–5). Ruth does what Naomi says, and at midnight Boaz wakes to find a woman at his feet, and she asks him to spread his skirt over her, because he is a near kinsman (Ruth 3:6–9). Boaz blesses her, says all the city knows she is a virtuous woman, and promises to do the part of a kinsman, but he says there is a kinsman nearer than he (Ruth 3:10–13). Ruth lies at his feet until morning and leaves before anyone can recognize her, and Boaz sends her home with six measures of barley (Ruth 3:14–17). Naomi tells her to sit still until she sees how the matter will fall, because Boaz will not rest until it is settled (Ruth 3:18).
Ruth 3.whereWeAre: In chapter 2, Boaz protected Ruth through the harvest, and Naomi learned he is a near kinsman. Here Ruth asks him to act as a family redeemer, but he says a closer relative must be asked first. Chapter 4 brings the matter to the city gate.

keyFigures.name: Ruth
keyFigures.role: Follows Naomi's plan, goes to the threshing floor, and asks Boaz to spread his skirt over her.

keyFigures.name: Naomi
keyFigures.role: Plans for Ruth to find rest and tells her to sit still until the matter is settled.

keyFigures.name: Boaz
keyFigures.role: Calls Ruth a virtuous woman and promises to act, but says a nearer kinsman comes first.

keyThemes.explanation: Naomi wants Ruth to have rest, "that it may be well with thee," and sends her to Boaz.
Ruth goes to the threshing floor at night and asks for Boaz's protection. He answers with kindness and calls her "a virtuous woman."
Boaz says "there is a kinsman nearer than I," so he will not skip the nearer man, but he promises to see it done.
Ruth goes home with six measures of barley, and Naomi tells her to sit still until the matter is settled.

Ruth 4.summary: Boaz goes up to the gate, sits down, calls the nearer kinsman over, and gathers ten elders of the city as witnesses (Ruth 4:1–2). He tells the kinsman that Naomi is selling Elimelech's land and that he has the first right to redeem it, and the man says, "I will redeem it" (Ruth 4:3–4). Boaz adds that whoever buys the field must also buy Ruth the Moabitess, "to raise up the name of the dead," so the kinsman says he cannot redeem it, "lest I mar mine own inheritance," and gives Boaz his shoe to confirm it (Ruth 4:5–8). Boaz tells the elders and all the people that they are witnesses that he has bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's, and Mahlon's, and that he has bought Ruth to be his wife, and the people bless him (Ruth 4:9–12). Boaz takes Ruth, the LORD gives her conception, and she bears a son, and the women tell Naomi he will restore her life and care for her in her old age (Ruth 4:13–15). Naomi becomes his nurse, and the neighbors name him Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David (Ruth 4:16–17). The book ends with the generations of Pharez down to David (Ruth 4:18–22).
Ruth 4.whereWeAre: In chapter 3, Ruth asked Boaz for help, and he promised to settle the matter. Here Boaz redeems the family land, marries Ruth, and Obed is born. The genealogy at the end leads to David, whose story begins in 1 Samuel.

keyFigures.name: Boaz
keyFigures.role: Settles the matter at the gate, buys Elimelech's land, and takes Ruth as his wife.

keyFigures.name: Ruth
keyFigures.role: Marries Boaz and bears Obed, who becomes David's grandfather.

keyFigures.name: Naomi
keyFigures.role: Takes the child, lays him in her bosom, and becomes his nurse.

keyFigures.name: The nearer kinsman
keyFigures.role: Says he cannot redeem the land "lest I mar mine own inheritance" and gives Boaz his shoe.

keyFigures.name: The elders and the people at the gate
keyFigures.role: Stand as witnesses and bless Boaz.

keyFigures.name: The women of Bethlehem
keyFigures.role: Praise the LORD with Naomi and name the child Obed.

keyThemes.explanation: Boaz settles the matter at the gate before ten elders, so everyone can see it done fairly.
Boaz buys Elimelech's land and takes Ruth as his wife, "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance."
The people at the gate bless Boaz, and the women of Bethlehem bless the LORD with Naomi.
Naomi, who said the LORD brought her home "empty," now holds Obed, who will restore her life and care for her in old age.
